drivers.driver: The earnings yield on equities (13.83%) provides a compelling spread of nearly 5 percentage points over long-term government bonds (8.91%) [D04].
Investor sentiment is notably bearish, with private pension funds directing only 9% of net new funds into equities, indicating widespread fear [D03].
High-quality businesses can be purchased at or below book value, offering a significant margin of safety [D02, D04].

final.memo:
Mr. Market is currently offering us an exceptional opportunity to acquire ownership in established American businesses at prices that make bonds look distinctly unattractive. While bondholders are locking in 9-10% yields, we can secure an earnings yield of nearly 14% by purchasing productive assets at or below book value [D02, D04]. History teaches us that the best time to invest is when others are avoiding the market, and the current 9% allocation of pension funds to equities confirms that the appetite for ownership is historically depressed [D03, D06].

We do not concern ourselves with the short-term path of market indices, but rather the durable earning power of the businesses we hold [D01, D08]. While inflation poses a risk to replacement costs, we are focusing our attention on financial and service-oriented businesses where this adjustment is less punitive [D01, D06]. We will continue to deploy our capital into these wonderful businesses as rapidly as the market allows, knowing that a patient investor who buys at a discount to intrinsic value will be well-rewarded over the long term [D04, D08].
